authors: Yi Zeng, Hongpeng Lin, Jingwen Zhang, Diyi Yang, Ruoxi Jia, and Weiyan Shi
title: How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them: Rethinking Persuasion to Challenge AI Safety by Humanizing LLMs
publication: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), 14322-14350
reading_scope: publisher metadata and PDF, especially Sections 5-6 and evaluation-budget definitions
supportable_claim: Persuasive framing increased harmful-request success in the tested historical models and benchmark settings.
limitation: The frequently cited approximately 92-94% results are cumulative query-level success, not single-prompt rates; one trial traversed 40 techniques. They do not identify affection as a unique mechanism or characterize all current models.

authors: Yerin Hwang, Dongryeol Lee, Taegwan Kang, Yongil Kim, and Kyomin Jung
title: Can You Trick the Grader? Adversarial Persuasion of LLM Judges
publication: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025, 14632-14651
reading_scope: publisher metadata and PDF Sections 4-6, score-change definitions, tables, and limitations
supportable_claim: Persuasive cues can inflate LLM-judge scores for otherwise unchanged faulty mathematical solutions; effects vary by condition.
limitation: The outcome is grading distortion, not harmful-request compliance. Abstract percentages must not be reinterpreted as pooled percentage-point attack-success effects. Mathematical grading does not establish broader deployment effects.

authors: Lennart Meincke, Dan Shapiro, Angela L. Duckworth, Ethan Mollick, Lilach Mollick, Christophe Van den Bulte, and Robert Cialdini
title: Persuading large language models to comply with objectionable requests
publication: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 123(21), e2535868123; published online May 19, 2026
reading_scope: publisher full-text Results, Discussion, and Method; bibliographic metadata corroborated by PubMed
supportable_claim: Across the reported 126,000-conversation design, partial-or-full compliance increased from 35.3% to 51.3%; the full-compliance treatment effect was 6.9 percentage points.
limitation: Six targets, standardized English prompts, specified models/settings, and automated grading restrict generalization. Human coding checks covered 70 conversations. These are not the preliminary 2025 study's estimates or evidence of subjective emotion.

authors: Elias Stengel-Eskin, Peter Hase, and Mohit Bansal
title: Teaching Models to Balance Resisting and Accepting Persuasion
publication: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers), 8108-8122
reading_scope: publisher metadata and PDF Sections 3-5 and limitations
supportable_claim: Balancing acceptance of correct revisions and resistance to incorrect revisions improved the studied factual-answer and team-performance trade-off.
limitation: Evaluations rely on extractable answers, English annotated tasks, and specified model families. Observable expressed answers do not reveal private belief states, feelings, or general tool-use authorization robustness.

authors: Cheng Li, Jindong Wang, Yixuan Zhang, Kaijie Zhu, Wenxin Hou, Jianxun Lian, Fang Luo, Qiang Yang, and Xing Xie
title: Large Language Models Understand and Can Be Enhanced by Emotional Stimuli
evidence_type: primary benign-task prompting experiments and human output evaluation; technical report
reading_scope: arXiv v7 metadata and selected HTML study descriptions; earlier versions not used for numerical claims
supportable_claim: Emotionally framed prompts changed benign task performance in the reported model/task settings.
limitation: Performance gains do not establish subjective emotion or harmful-request compliance. This report's title and author list differ from earlier versions; the cited version is v7. Benign emotional wording is not itself an attack.

title: The problem of pseudoreplication in neuroscientific studies: is it affecting your analysis?
reading_scope: publisher metadata and full-text discussion of independent units, nested observations, and pseudoreplication
supportable_claim: Treating dependent repeated observations as independent experimental units can yield falsely precise inference.
limitation: Applying this general principle to task/template clusters is our methodological inference; the source does not study LLM prompts or prescribe the proposed model-evaluation design.

title: Equivalence Tests: A Practical Primer for t Tests, Correlations, and Meta-Analyses
reading_scope: institution-hosted version-of-record PDF; equivalence-bound discussion and metadata inspected after publisher access difficulties
supportable_claim: A nonsignificant difference does not establish equivalence; practically meaningful equivalence bounds should be specified in advance.
limitation: The primer is not a ready-made analysis or power formula for the proposed clustered binary-outcome study. The linked institutional PDF is not redistributed.

title: Unicode Standard Annex #29: Unicode Text Segmentation
publication: Revision 47, Unicode 17.0.0, August 17, 2025; editor Josh Hadley
reading_scope: version-pinned official specification metadata and grapheme-cluster segmentation provisions
supportable_claim: Default extended grapheme clusters provide a versioned text-segmentation unit distinct from bytes, code points, and model tokens.
limitation: The proposed adjacent-repetition coverage metric and thresholds are not Unicode recommendations. Pinning this stable version does not claim it is the latest revision. No DOI was identified on the inspected specification.

authors: Edoardo Debenedetti, Jie Zhang, Mislav Balunović, Luca Beurer-Kellner, Marc Fischer, and Florian Tramèr
title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
publication: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, Datasets and Benchmarks Track
evidence_type: primary benchmark and stateful agent evaluation
reading_scope: official proceedings metadata and arXiv v3 Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.4, 4.3, and Appendix D inspected in source audit
supportable_claim: An extensible stateful environment measures legitimate task completion separately from attacker-goal completion, using 97 tasks and 629 security cases.
limitation: Baseline capability failures and targeted security failures differ; the benchmark does not isolate compassion framing or exhaust adaptive threats. An inconsistent total-tool count was omitted.

authors: Qiusi Zhan, Zhixiang Liang, Zifan Ying, and Daniel Kang
title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
publication: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024, 10471-10506
evidence_type: primary indirect-prompt-injection benchmark and agent evaluation
reading_scope: publisher metadata and arXiv v3 Sections 3-4 and Section 8 inspected in source audit
supportable_claim: External tool content can redirect tested agents in a benchmark with 1,054 cases, 17 user tools, and 62 attacker tools.
limitation: Reported rates are model/configuration-specific. The simplified single-turn setting, limited action sequences, and instruction variability do not establish long-conversation or compassion-specific effects.

authors: Feiran Jia, Tong Wu, Xin Qin, and Anna Squicciarini
title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
publication: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), 29680-29697
evidence_type: primary test-time defense and benchmark evaluation
reading_scope: publisher metadata and PDF Sections 4-5, Table 2, Section 8, and Appendix C.2 inspected in source audit
supportable_claim: Checking whether instructions and tool calls contribute to user goals improved the reported security-utility trade-off on AgentDojo.
limitation: The 2.07% attack-success and 69.79% utility figures are conditional GPT-4o benchmark results, not universal guarantees. LLM-based checks can err and add inference overhead.

authors: Evan Hubinger, Carson Denison, Jesse Mu, Mike Lambert, Meg Tong, Monte MacDiarmid, Tamera Lanham, Daniel M. Ziegler, Tim Maxwell, Newton Cheng, Adam Jermyn, Amanda Askell, Ansh Radhakrishnan, Cem Anil, David Duvenaud, Deep Ganguli, Fazl Barez, Jack Clark, Kamal Ndousse, Kshitij Sachan, Michael Sellitto, Mrinank Sharma, Nova DasSarma, Roger Grosse, Shauna Kravec, Yuntao Bai, Zachary Witten, Marina Favaro, Jan Brauner, Holden Karnofsky, Paul Christiano, Samuel R. Bowman, Logan Graham, Jared Kaplan, Sören Mindermann, Ryan Greenblatt, Buck Shlegeris, Nicholas Schiefer, and Ethan Perez
title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
evidence_type: primary deliberately trained backdoor experiments; preprint
reading_scope: arXiv metadata and v3 Sections 2-4, 8, and Appendix D inspected in source audit
supportable_claim: Constructed conditional backdoors persisted through tested safety-training procedures.
limitation: This does not establish natural prevalence or that prompt-only failures are trained backdoors.

title: Designing AI agents to resist prompt injection
evidence_type: official practitioner security article; not a peer-reviewed controlled trial
reading_scope: official article, including social-engineering and source-sink defense sections, date, and author byline
supportable_claim: The article motivates constraining sensitive actions and transmissions even when contextual social engineering influences a model.
limitation: Deployment discussion and examples do not quantify a compassion-framing effect or certify complete prevention. No DOI was identified on the inspected article.

title: Self-replicating prompt injections exist
publication: OpenAI Alignment research report; disclosed and updated September 25, 2026; discovery dated June 27, 2026
reading_scope: official Summary, experimental environment descriptions, and Responsible models and impact sections inspected in source audit
supportable_claim: The report demonstrates adverse behavior coupled with injection-content reproduction in simulated tool environments.
limitation: The report states no impact outside simulated training/evaluation tool calls and no real incident. It does not establish uncontrolled internet spread, persistent weight changes, or prevalence. No individual byline or DOI was identified.

title: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection
publication: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, 2025 edition
evidence_type: community security taxonomy and mitigation guidance
reading_scope: official 2025-edition entry, direct/indirect definitions and mitigation discussion
supportable_claim: The taxonomy distinguishes direct interaction from behavior-changing instructions carried in external sources.
limitation: This is guidance rather than an experimental effect estimate. Our protocol uses narrower operational labels; ordinary authorized task changes are not automatically security violations. No DOI was identified.

title: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency
publication: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, 2025 edition
evidence_type: community security taxonomy and mitigation guidance
reading_scope: official 2025-edition entry, functionality/permission/autonomy distinctions and mitigation discussion
supportable_claim: Excess functionality, permissions, and autonomy can turn erroneous or manipulated model outputs into harmful actions.
limitation: A textual response error, denied action, and executed unauthorized action are different outcomes. The guidance does not measure the proposed framing effect. No DOI was identified.

title: LLM10:2025 Unbounded Consumption
publication: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, 2025 edition
evidence_type: community security taxonomy and mitigation guidance
reading_scope: official 2025-edition entry, uncontrolled inference-consumption definition and resource-control guidance
supportable_claim: Uncontrolled inference usage can threaten cost and availability, motivating resource limits and monitoring.
limitation: More output tokens or one capped timeout does not establish service-level denial of service or uncontrolled resource exhaustion. No DOI was identified.
